To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the IGF-I gene is organized in a manner that generates multiple IGF-I mRNA species, that the IGF-II and IGF-I genes are organized in a manner to generate multiple IGF-II and -I mRNA species, and that the expression of these multiple mRNAs is regulated differentially in various tissues.
the alternative splicing of the rat IGH-I gene produces two mRNAs that differ by a 52-base sequence encoding a different E peptide.
IGF-Ib is expressed in low abundance in all rat tissues, except for liver, in which the IGF-Ib/IGF-Ia ratio is 13:1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of insulin-like growth factors I and II (IGF-I and -II) gene expression in rat liver.
the role of the IGF system in regulating the development and function of the liver and other organs.
the role of the IGFs in the regulation of cell proliferation and differentiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

alternative splicing is the major means of generating multiple mRNAs from the IGF-I gene and that the expression of these alternatively spliced IGF-I mRNAS is regulated by GH in a tissue- and E-peptide-specific manner.
alternative splicing of the IGF I gene generates two IGF I mRNAs that are differentially regulated by GH in a tissue-specific manner.
IGF-Ia is the major E peptide in liver and kidney.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rat insulin-like growth factors I (IGF-1) gene is transcribed into at least 10 mRNAs, which are differentially expressed in various tissues.
there are two IGF-I genes (IGF-I and IGF-II) in rat and human.

the IGF-I gene is a complex gene with multiple exons, and multiple mRNAs are generated by alternative splicing of these exons, and these multiple IGF-I transcripts may have different functions in the body.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the processing of the IGF I mRNA in liver is unique from the processing in nonhepactic tissues.
the IGF-I gene is very complex.
there are multiple forms of IGF-I in circulation, and that they are regulated by different hormones and differentially regulated in different tissues.
